chunks: It is He who sends down the rain when they had despaired of it, and spreads His mercy. He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about Allah sending rain after people have despaired?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of divine grace intervening at the precise moment of human despair, reflecting the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt as the 'Wali' who facilitate spiritual and physical sustenance. The transition from 'qanatu' (despair) to 'yanshuru rahmatahu' (spreading mercy) underscores the theological principle that divine favor is not bound by human limitation but is activated by His will. This reinforces the attribute of Al-Hamid, acknowledging that all blessings, including the rain of mercy, originate from the Praiseworthy One.
